en.title: Maximum Subjects Passed with Limited Extra Answers
en.description:
Each subject already has answered[i] questions answered correctly, and passing requires at least needed[i]. You may answer at most q more questions correctly in total, distributed among the subjects in any way; maximize the number of subjects passed.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n q, the second line contains answered, and the third line contains needed. 1≤n≤100000; 0≤(each element),q≤10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: the first two subjects need 27+25=52 questions, so 2 subjects can be passed; all three subjects would need 152 questions, which exceeds the budget. Example 2: add 1 question to the second subject to pass 1 subject. Example 3: both subjects already meet the requirement, so no extra answers are needed and the answer is 2.
hints: Compute each subject's non-negative shortfall, sort ascending, and pay starting from the cheapest subject.
